          I.              WITNESS IDENTIFICATION

 1   Q:        PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND OCCUPATION.

 2   A:        My name is Mark Garrett. I am the President of Garrett Group Consulting, Inc., a firm

 3             specializing in public utility regulation, litigation, and consulting services.

 4

 5   Q:        PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND YOUR

 6             PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE RELATED TO UTILITY REGULATION?

 7   A:        I am a licensed attorney and a certified public accountant. I work as a consultant in public

 8             utility regulation. I received my bachelor’s degree from the University of Oklahoma and

 9             completed post-graduate hours at Stephen F. Austin State University and at the University

10             of Texas at Arlington and Pan American. I received my Juris Doctor from Oklahoma City

11             University Law School and was admitted to the Oklahoma Bar in 1997. I am a Certified

12             Public Accountant licensed in Texas and Oklahoma, with a background in public

13             accounting, industry, and utility regulation.

14                    In public accounting, as a staff auditor for a firm in Dallas, I primarily audited

15             financial institutions in the State of Texas. In private industry, as controller for a mid-

16             sized ($300 million) corporation in Dallas, I managed the accounting function, including

17             general ledger, accounts payable, financial reporting, audits, tax returns, budgets,

18             projections, and supervision of accounting personnel. In utility regulation, I served as an

19             auditor in the Public Utility Division of the Oklahoma Corporation Commission (OCC)

20             from 1991 to 1995. In that position, I managed the audits of major gas and electric utility

 2               Since my departure from the OCC, I have worked on numerous rate cases and other

 3        regulatory proceedings on behalf of various consumers, consumer groups, public utility

 4        commissions staff, and offices of attorneys general. I have provided testimony before the

 5        public utility commissions in Alaska, Arizona, Arkansas, Colorado, Florida, Indiana,

 6        Kansas, Massachusetts, Nevada, New Mexico, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee,

 7        Texas, Utah, and Washington. My clients include industrial customers, hospitals,

10        issue of incentive compensation, and as a regular instructor at the New Mexico State

     II.   PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY AND SUMMARY OF ADJUSTMENTS

4    Q:    WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

5    A:    I offer testimony regarding various revenue requirement issues. I also sponsor the

6          CLC/DAC revenue requirement exhibits.

7

8    Q:    WHAT RATE INCREASE IS THE COMPANY PROPOSING IN THIS

9          PROCEEDING?

10   A:    EPE proposes an increase of $70,482,824 in its amended application. This increase, if

11         approved, would result in a staggering 50.5% increase in rates. Based on my experience,

12         a standard benchmark for “rate shock” to customers occurs when utility rates increase in

13         excess of 10%. An increase of 50.5% results in extreme rate shock which indicates the

14         need for regulatory mitigation. In light of the affordability crisis facing customers, I

15         recommend that the Commission accept every reasonable adjustment available to mitigate

16         the proposed increase and then cap the increase at no more than 20% over a 2-year phase-

17         in period.

18

19   Q:    PLEASE SUMMARIZE THE REVENUE REQUIREMENT ADJUSTMENTS.

20   A:    A summary of the CLC/DAC adjustments is set forth below:

 1   Expense Adjustments

 2      •   Accelerated Depreciation of Newman and Montana Plants: I recommend that

 3          the Commission reject EPE’s request to accelerate the depreciation of these plants.

 4          The Company has not demonstrated how these generating units will ultimately be

 5          retired, repurposed, or replaced. Commission precedent in Case No. 21-00017-UT

 6          establishes that retirement decisions should not be approved without sufficient

 7          information regarding replacement resources and their effect on reliable service.

 8      •   Short-Term Incentive (“STIP”) Compensation: I recommend removing all

 9          STIP costs from rates because the Company’s plan rewards financial and

10          operational metrics that either primarily benefit shareholders or represent existing

11          obligations of a regulated utility. This adjustment is $770,518.

12      •   Payroll Expense: I recommend accepting annualized wages through September

13          30, 2025, but removing unsupported non-union wage escalations and using the

14          base-year payroll expense ratio. These adjustments reduce New Mexico payroll

15          expense by $1,003,731 and yield an additional payroll tax reduction of $119,653.

16      •   COVID-19 Deferred Costs: I recommend amortizing deferred COVID-19 costs

17          over five years rather than two years. This adjustment reduces the annual New

18          Mexico revenue requirement by $1,222,668.

19      •   Rate Case Expense: I recommend limiting recoverable rate case costs to $1.630

20          million, amortizing those costs over five years, and excluding rate case costs from

21          rate base. These adjustments reduce the revenue requirement by $681,900.

 1   •   Dues and Membership Expense: I recommend disallowing 100% of the

 2       Company’s Edison Electric Institute (“EEI”) membership dues because the

 3       Company has not demonstrated that these costs are necessary to provide regulated

 4       utility service or that this membership provides measurable benefits to customers.

 5       I further recommend a 50% -50% sharing of remaining dues and membership costs

 6       in recognition of the fact that these are discretionary expenditures that are not

 7       essential to the provision of electric service and are of significant benefit to

 8       shareholders.

 9   •   Advertising Expense: I recommend disallowance of the Company’s advertising

10       expenses directly allocated to New Mexico. The Company has not met its burden

11       under Rule 350 to demonstrate that its directly allocated advertising costs are

12       reasonable or that the costs incurred provide benefits to customers. This adjustment

13       reduces the annual New Mexico revenue requirement by $461,267.

14   •   Regulatory Asset Amortization: To address the affordability crisis faced by

15       EPE’s customers and to mitigate the rate impacts of the Company’s requested

16       overall revenue requirement I recommend amortizing deferred regulatory assets

17       over five years rather than two years as recommended by the Company, which

18       reduces annual New Mexico revenue requirement by $419,683.

19   •   Meter Reading Expenses: I recommend disallowances of the Company’s meter

20       reading expense in the amount of $658,837 and testing expense in the amount of

21       $36,537.

 1   Rate Base and Purchased Capacity Adjustments

 2      •   Post-Test-Year Plant Additions: I recommend that the Commission deny the

 3          Company’s request to recover post-test-year capacity purchases. Allowing

 4          recovery of base rate increases after the test year, in a vacuum, without offsetting

 5          adjustments for accumulated depreciation, accumulated deferred taxes and load

 6          growth during the same period, would constitute piecemeal ratemaking and

 7          circumvent the comprehensive review afforded in a general rate case.            This

 8          adjustment reduces the Company’s proposed increase by $16,995,566.

 9      •   Cash Working Capital: I recommend including long-term debt interest expense

10          in the Company’s lead-lag study because it is a cash expense collected from

11          customers before it is paid to creditors, and the utility uses this money to fund its

12          day to day operations. This adjustment reduces the New Mexico rate base by

13          $3,672,808 and the revenue requirement by $385,847.

14   Adjustments Proposed by Other CLC/ DAC Witnesses

15      •   Cost of Capital: I incorporate the return on equity and capital structure

16          recommendations of Mr. David Garrett in revenue requirement calculations. These

17          recommendations reduce the revenue requirement by $17,364,903.

18      •   Depreciation: I also incorporate the depreciation expense adjustments

19          recommended by Mr. David Garrett in the revenue requirement schedules. These

20          recommendations reduce the revenue requirement by $4,863,894.

     III.        THE AFFORDABILITY CRISIS FACING CUSTOMERS

 1   Q:         DO YOU BELIEVE THE RATE INCREASE REQUESTED BY THE COMPANY

 2              IS NECESSARY FOR THE PROVISION OF ELECTRIC SERVICE?

 3   A:         No. In this proceeding, EPE has requested a $70.4 million increase, which, if approved,

 4              would raise rates by 50.5%, and would result in a 73.37% increase to base rates for the

 5              residential customer class. 1 Although the Company contends these increases are necessary

 6              for grid infrastructure investment, the rate increase is also being driven by the Company’s

 7              excessive requested return on equity (ROE) of 10.7%, an equity rich capital structure of

 8              55.5% equity to 44.5% debt, and several O&M expenditures that are not appropriate for a

 9              regulated utility and not necessary for the provision of utility service. These expenditures

10              are discussed in more detail in the sections below, but it is apparent that the Company did

11              very little to mitigate its requested rate increase.


12   Q:         HAVE RATEPAYERS IN NEW MEXICO EXPRESSED CONCERN ABOUT THE

13              AFFORDABILITY CRISIS?

15              Paso Electric’s requested rate increase in this proceeding. According to these articles,
